messages:
maria: Quick note — we just ran a query and noticed variant attribution mismatch between SDK clients and server-side splits for the canary. Looks like ~7% of traffic had no x-redwood-variant and ended up in default bucket.
jon: Oof. Do we know if it's a rollout config problem or the SDK not sending header? any OS / platform skew?
maria: Mostly iOS 14.6 and older Android webviews. SDK logs show the header was absent for those requests.
kevin: SDK currently injects header only after feature flag evaluation. If the client fails evaluation (timeout or missing config) it omits header instead of sending an explicit "none" variant.
anya: That explains it — server interprets missing header as server-side routing fallback which picks the production model. We should make client explicitly send a variant like `none` or `client-unavailable` so attribution is deterministic.
jon: +1. Also we need telemetry counters for three states: client-variant-present, client-variant-none, server-assigned. Right now dashboards mix them and our A/B metrics are polluted.
sre-bot: Incident note: previous regression alert fired because 5xx rate rose 0.4% during rollout window. Not directly correlated but worth checking.
kevin: Proposed changes:

1) SDK: always send `x-redwood-variant` header. If client couldn't evaluate, send `x-redwood-variant: _client_unset`.
2) SDK: send `x-redwood-variant-source: client|server` so we can distinguish.
3) Server: treat `_client_unset` as a valid token and route to server policy only if explicit fallback rule applies.
4) Telemetry: emit `rollout.variant_source` tag in traces and increment counters `rollout.variant.client`, `.server`, `.unset`.

anya: Sounds good. One UX question: should Console rollout UI show "client opt-out" as a separate bucket when configuring splits? Right now you can only configure server buckets.
ui-lead: We should. From product POV people want to know how much traffic is being evaluated client-side vs server-side. UI could show a small gauge: "Client-evaluated: 12%" with breakdown by variant.
maria: Also need guards: if SDK version < 1.2 (no source header), server should backfill variant_source=client_legacy to avoid losing signal.
kevin: Implementation plan: add header and source in SDK 1.3. Add server acceptance for `_client_unset` immediately and start counting. Backfill/compat fallback in server for v<1.2. Rollout: canary to 5% of clients then 25% then 100%.
jon: How do we detect client version? We already get `user-agent` and `x-redwood-sdk-version` in requests. Use that.
anya: For telemetry naming, agree use `rollout.variant.source` and `rollout.variant.name`. Keep labels short for time-series cardinality.
ui-lead: For console, add new column in rollouts table: "client-eval rate" and an icon showing if any legacy clients are present.
sre-bot: Reminder: any header change must be documented in the API changelog and listed in our CORS-safe headers.
kevin: Good catch. Also add tests: unit test for header present/missing, e2e asserting telemetry counters, and an integration test where SDK sends `_client_unset` and server routes to server_default bucket.
maria: I'll open a PR for the SDK change and a separate server PR. Can someone add the console mockups? ui-lead?
ui-lead: I'll sketch a mock by EOD and add to the rollout UX epic.
jon: For rollout guardrails: add a safety policy that if server sees >2x error rate in client-assigned variants within 5m, automatically shift traffic to server-default and notify oncall.
anya: Agree. Also link the telemetry to Quality alerts so eng knows if a variant causes regressions.
maria: Thanks team. I'll capture action items:
- maria: PR for SDK header and source (target: canary 5%)
- kevin: server acceptance + telemetry counters
- anya: metrics names and dashboard widgets
- ui-lead: console mockups and rollout UI change
- jon: add guard policy and alerting

maria: tagging folks: @jon @kevin @anya @ui-lead. Will follow up with PR links.
